name: BACH_0377
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (88%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, second model agrees, input not flagged.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 88%, Invasive 12% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | InSitu only (90%) | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 1.00 / 94th percentile | Not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 InSitu | Mixed; two Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (regions 5, 6) · ↑ invasive · Associated with invasion; strongest in these regions · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 1, 6, 9) · ↑ invasive · Associated with invasion; strongest in these regions · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 4, 5) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood · Weak
- **Tumor cell fraction and density** (regions 5, 6) · context · Fraction 74% (97th percentile); density at reference maximum [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions beats random (+0.54 logit, CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis (3/20) and mitoses (0/20) are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Two of five similar cases are Invasive, and invasive probability is 12%.
- Validated stroma and pleomorphism concepts lean invasive; the in situ call may understate invasion.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 8, 9**: Highest heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for stromal invasion.
2. **Regions 5, 6**: Check stroma for tumor extending beyond duct walls.
3. **Regions 4, 5**: Confirm atypical cells stay confined within ducts.
